analysis.title: Chart of the Day - What Will Matter for the AI Trade
key_insights: Construction put in place for data centers has hit new highs and year-to-date surpasses 2025's total dollar amount, despite moratoriums, bottlenecks, and negative consumer sentiment around the AI buildout.
During 3Q 2026 reporting season, fears over peak capex growth have weighed on markets and worries over incremental profitability have weighed on the AI complex.
Wolfe continues to believe demand for compute remains robust and viewed AMD and SMCI earnings results from the prior night as very solid.
Wolfe's sense is that Hinojosa's surprise victory in Texas and the subsequent Blue Wave across Congress spells trouble for the AI trade in the very short term.
Wolfe is watching whether stocks trade with fundamentals on 4 Nov or revert to choppy macro price action, and how new Texas governor Gina Hinojosa handles the ongoing pause in data center permitting.

sector_views.rationale: Demand for compute remains robust and data center construction is at new highs, though the Blue Wave in Congress is a short-term risk.

earnings_insights: AMD and SMCI 3Q 2026 earnings, reported the night of 3 Nov 2026, were viewed by Wolfe as very solid. The note gives no EPS or revenue figures.
risk_factors: Fears over peak AI capex growth.
Worries over incremental profitability of the AI buildout.
Political opposition to the AI buildout, including moratoriums and permitting pauses, with Texas as a possible model for opposition response.
Choppy macro price action overriding fundamentals in the short term.
geopolitical: Hinojosa's surprise victory in the Texas governor race and a subsequent Blue Wave across Congress.
Ongoing pause in data center permitting in Texas, which has one of the largest data center backlogs by power capacity.

tension_points.what_invalidates: Stocks reverting to choppy macro price action instead of trading with fundamentals after the solid earnings reports.
